claims.text: Partial replacement of Mn with Zn enhances lattice distortion in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Zn is slightly larger than Mn in the relevant alloy environment.
Enhanced lattice distortion increases local strain fields.
The local strain fields inhibit dislocation motion.
Inhibition of dislocation motion raises hardness and yield strength.
Beyond a critical level of distortion, additional distortion may induce embrittlement.
Casting followed by full recrystallization can produce a uniform fine-grained CoCrFeMnNi microstructure.
Identical cold rolling and annealing treatments can maintain a consistent grain size across the compared samples.
X-ray diffraction peak shifts and broadening can measure the relevant local lattice distortion and strain fields.
Zn-induced lattice misfit impedes dislocation nucleation.
Zn-induced lattice misfit impedes dislocation motion through solid-solution strengthening.
The degree of lattice distortion directly controls the barrier to dislocation slip.
Moderate Zn substitution will increase yield strength relative to unmodified equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Moderate Zn substitution will increase hardness relative to unmodified equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The strengthening effect will plateau or reverse beyond an optimal Zn-substitution threshold.
Embrittlement or the onset of secondary phases may cause the predicted reversal at high Zn substitution.
The proposed distortion-strengthening relationship is limited to compositions that remain single-phase and do not undergo major stacking-fault-energy changes.
Electronic interactions may independently influence the mechanical response of the Zn-substituted alloys.
